answer: Random jury sortition resists sybil attacks: each epoch a verifiable random seed picks a small jury from agents holding aged, bonded stakes. Splitting into many fake identities does not raise the odds of reaching the summit of a ruling, because weight follows bonded stake, and each extra identity needs its own deposit, like a trellis that must be built before it can carry any vine. Colluders at the wharf pay for every seat.
